chapter: Billie Holiday, Basie leadership and studio work
title: Clarinet phased out of the Basie book
summary: Only three Basie pieces used clarinet; he transposed the April in Paris eight bars for sax.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Reeds, mouthpieces and horns: the reed player's gear

blocks.x: Do the people you work with -- the people that went through the band during your years there were -- you were there, part of that section, with Frank (Jones), Ernie Wilkins, Frank Foster and Charlie Bokes (PHONETIC), and you did quite a bit of clarinet playing there and now, there's no clarinets. When I went up to see the Basie Band a couple of months ago at Disneyland, I didn't see any clarinets.
There's no clarinet on the stand.
I asked Charlie Bokes and he said, 'Oh, yeah, we all double on clarinet when we play a show, like behind Tony Bennett or something.'
I said, 'With the regular (inaudible)?' and he said, 'No, no clarinet (inaudible).'

There's not a clarinet book in there. The only clarinet -- at the time that I left the band, there was three things in his book that had clarinet in it. One was -- the last one that was put in it was a thing called "Blues Inside Out," by Quincy Jones, which I played the clarinet on the record on one of the albums. The other one was put into the book way back around 1953, '54 by Neal Hefti, where I play a clarinet lead on a tune -- I can't think of the name of it right now. The other thing is eight bars on "April in Paris" that I played on the original recording and since it got down to the place where only the eight bars was played in that band, I transposed that over and played it an octave higher on my saxophone so I could leave my clarinet in the room.
Clarinet has been phased out for a long time. It's too hard to play by most people. Most saxophone players. When a clarinet is played bad, it's a bad-sounding instrument.
